name: Calibration assumptions
statement: For the 'estimated' calibration, the scatter per record (σe) and the shift per group (σu) are estimated by code from each analysis's frozen records with Henderson's method III, fixed at the rules lock: fit the locked model (RSS_R, rank r_R) and the same model with one intercept per group (RSS_F, rank r_F); σe² = RSS_F / (N - r_F); σu² = max(0, (RSS_R - RSS_F - (r_F - r_R) σe²) / tr(Z'M_R Z)). A negative estimate set to zero is recorded with its value before truncation. Not estimable (N <= r_F, RSS_F zero, or the trace zero): the estimated calibration of that analysis is 'unavailable' with the reason, and the fixed one is still reported. No person or agent chooses a value. A flag, never a gate.

name: What no plan can ever do to the primary set
statement: These hold for every plan, including any plan written by a model; no plan setting can change them. (1) An exact duplicate is never counted twice: one record of the group, chosen by the survivor rule, enters. (2) No record connected to a definite conflict ever enters, under any plan: not both records, not one. That includes a record linked by exact duplicates to a record in conflict (the whole connected group stays out). A survivor's value is counted only in the sensitivity analysis 'conflicts_survivor_value'. (3) A physically invalid value never enters. (4) A group whose identity cannot be resolved (several candidates) never enters; it is counted separately only in the sensitivity analysis 'possible_duplicates_separate'. (5) A model-recalled record never enters. (6) A constructed record (the controlled extract) never enters a run that is not marked as a test. (7) A record without a group under the plan's grouping never enters (no group is invented; entry 'records_without_group'). A plan that tries (1) to (4) is refused at the rules lock and refused again when its rules are applied; (5) is refused by the database; (6) by code at record storage, inclusion and the freeze; (7) by the eligibility rule 'group_unknown'. The one plan choice that remains: possible duplicates counted once (the default) or both counted. They are also enforced on the frozen set itself: at the dataset freeze, code checks the primary set against each of (1) to (7), using the Checks flags (paper identity and physical validity computed independently of the plan's grouping and outcome) and each record's kind, source and, for (7), group under the plan's grouping, and refuses the freeze, logging the refusal, if any fails.

statement: A Curator proposal passes only if, in this order (`quotes.check`): (1) the value is allowed: a vocabulary value, a microstructure of vocabulary tokens joined by '+', or for the test temperature a finite number of °C (never JSON null, a boolean or a string); (2) the quote is 30 to 600 characters after collapsing runs of whitespace; (3) it occurs in one of the sealed version's documentation files after collapsing runs of whitespace on both sides (nothing else normalized: no case folding, no markup changes), beginning and ending at a word boundary there, code finding the document and the line; (4) it holds a listed term for the value (TERMS) as a whole word, after collapsing whitespace and setting aside 'ultimate tensile strength' (so 'tensile' there alone is not a test type), case-insensitive except B2 and L12; a microstructure joined by '+' needs every part; a test temperature is a complete signed number (sign and decimals included; no leading zero) equal to the value, never part of a larger number ('1,025', '1 025') and never an end of a range ('20 - 25', '20–25', '20 to 25', '20 °C to 25 °C'), followed by a Celsius unit in a form found in the frozen documents ('°C', after spaces or LaTeX '~', or LaTeX '\SI{n}{\degreeCelsius}'); (5) for a test condition (test type, temperature band, test temperature) it also holds a testing word as a whole word (test, tests, tested, testing, loaded, loading, strain rate), so a processing sentence such as 'cold rolled at room temperature' or 'deformed by cold rolling at room temperature' is refused. name: What happens when an agent request fails
statement: Every agent request is reserved, sent once (litellm's retries off) outside any database transaction, and recorded. At most two requests per agent call: an unavailable provider (connection error, timeout, 429, 5xx, or a reply litellm cannot read) is tried once more with the same request; an unusable answer (empty, malformed, a tool call, truncated at the output limit, longer than the role allows) once more with a fixed corrective note naming only the failure code; refused credentials (401, 403), another refused request (4xx), a refusal, a cost the provider did not report, a reservation that cannot be written (nothing is sent), a failed recording on any branch (after a provider failure, a reply without usage or a usable reply) and every spending refusal stop at once. A failed call is recorded with no usage and counts at its maximum cost; a call whose recording fails stays 'started' and counts at its maximum cost. No provider, library or database text is kept with a call or sent in a later request; the process log gets the failure code, the exception's types and where it was raised, never its text. Not covered: what a library logs by itself (litellm's own debug logging is off unless a process turns it on). DSPy's JSON fallback is off. Step 8b: a role's own check of an answer that could be read gives a code that is corrected once the same way: 'invalid_plan' (Planner), 'numbers_unmatched' and 'wording_refused' (Analyst). The Analyst's 'unknown_name' and 'digit_outside_placeholder' are corrected once the same way.

It gives: the question as asked (the claim's words) and as tested (register 'question_as_tested'); the outcome and verdict wording (with the label, exploratory or 'data found; not enough to test'); the evidence level with its wording; when an estimate is shown, the model sentence, the pooled estimate with its unit, its standard error, the p-value phrase, the record and alloy counts and the four paper figures together, the direction note, the spread of the slope information ('an effective number of groups of E out of N informative groups; largest share S', always with an inference, no threshold, never compared with a minimum), the group definition, one sensitivity line (sets in agreement, range of estimates with units) and the calibration summary; a coefficient without inference is shown as the coefficient only. name: The run order and what a failure does to a run
statement: A run goes: Planner, narrowing decision (code), then either the partly-sufficient path or the rules lock, records, Checks, Critic, Inclusion, dataset freeze, statistics, Analyst and the copy of code's decision. A fixed-plan run bypasses the Planner (criterion 14.1a); so does a narrower question's run, recognised by its link to its original (its stored plan). A Planner failure, a domain mismatch, a claim that is not one plan, a refused checkpoint or write, changed source versions for a narrower question, and a spending refusal at the Planner or the Critic fail the run with a stated reason. A Critic failure leaves flags unclassified and the run goes on. Any Analyst failure, a spending refusal included, leaves code's decision standing: the run completes with 'explanation unavailable' (a departure from PRD 14.4's 'marked failed' for a cap reached at the Analyst, by the owner's decision). A recording or reservation failure at any agent stops the run at once: no further model request (no further Critic batch, no Analyst), nothing more written, no narrower question created; the run stays running (a call whose recording failed stays started) until step 9's recovery. No model call runs inside a database transaction.

history.value: Numbers shown to the Analyst (and, from step 10, to people) are rounded by code in one place: k, its standard error and t to 0.1; a p-value to two significant figures (scientific notation below 0.001, e.g. 1.3e-6); counts exact; the effective number of papers to two decimals; the largest share and every other share or rate (calibration, detection, power and their intervals) as a percentage to one decimal; temperatures, scatter and shift to at most one decimal; the threshold as given; any other number to three significant figures. A p-value is shown as 'p ≈ <value> (approximate, nominal, one-sided)'; the paper figures as '<n> informative papers, an effective number of papers of <e>, a largest share of <s> and <df> degrees of freedom'.
